name: pipe2-then-splice
why: pipe2() followed by splice(read-only file -> pipe) in the same pid within 5s is the DirtyPipe precondition correlation. On glibc 2.39 (the ubuntu-24.04 CI runner) pipe() is routed to pipe2(fds, 0), so the atomic emits pipe2 with a1=0
source: recorded: strace of dirtypipe_behavioral.c -- pipe2(ptr, 0) then splice(rfd=5, &off, p[1]=4, NULL, 1, 0). splice a1/a3 are off_in/off_out (off_in is a ptr here, off_out NULL=0); len=1 is a4, not logged; exit is the decimal byte count

name: pipe2-cloexec-then-splice
why: the pipe2(O_CLOEXEC) variant followed by splice() in one pid is the same correlation; the O_CLOEXEC flag bit (a1=0x80000) must not hide it
source: synthetic: a dropper using pipe2(O_CLOEXEC) then splice()

name: pipe2-only-no-splice
why: a shell pipeline creates a pipe but never splices; half the correlation, so the splice base must be required. (bash on glibc 2.39 issues pipe2(fds, 0), not the raw pipe syscall)
source: recorded: strace of `bash -c 'true | true'` on this host -- pipe2([3,4], 0)

name: haproxy-pooled-splice-no-pipe-in-window
why: HAProxy keeps a pipe pool and splices socket<->pipe for zero-copy forwarding; the splice(pipe -> socket) is a valid splice (one end is the pool pipe) but the pipe2 that filled the pool was created earlier, outside this 5s window, so only the splice is in-window. Half the correlation, so the pipe base must be required. (The prior case modelled splice(file -> socket), which the kernel rejects with EINVAL because neither end is a pipe -- an impossible success record.)
source: synthetic: HAProxy pooled-pipe zero-copy splice; fd_in=pool pipe read end, fd_out=socket

name: pipe-and-splice-different-pid
why: pipe2() in a parent and splice() in a forked child split the two syscalls across pids within 5s; the pid group-by must enforce same-process
source: synthetic: pipe2() in pid X, splice() in forked child pid Y

name: pipe-then-splice-too-late
why: the same pid does pipe2() and splice() but 30s apart, outside the 5s window; the timespan must bound the correlation
source: synthetic: a long-lived daemon that happens to pipe early and splice much later
